A.reason: All candidates respect the resource and privacy limits and check availability, condition, cleanup and seated access. Their primary mechanisms are centralized return processing, visible reshelving destinations, an on-site reserve, optional shared tidying and portable return reminders. Candidate 0 offers the clearest borrowing ritual and predictable volunteer workflow, with observable failure criteria.

B.reason: All candidates are usable without definite serious hard-constraint violations. Candidate 5 repairs candidate 0's centralized return mechanism with capacity limits and recovery gates; it is not a distinct mechanism. The other mechanisms are visible reshelving destinations, an on-site reserve, optional shared tidying, reader damage screening and controlled donation intake. Candidate 5 best addresses return overflow, temporary unavailability and the fixed volunteer budget while specifying measurable stop conditions.

pair.reason: B5 improves on A0 by checking return capacity before launch, limiting intake and explicitly stopping or reverting when overflow, access or workload fails. These concrete feasibility safeguards give it a modest advantage, despite added complexity and the fallback's reduced condition screening.
